ProductTitle: Batiste Dry Shampoo Fresh, Breezy Citrus Scent, Refreshes Hair Without Drying, 4.23 oz (Pack of 6)
ReviewTitle: Love this dry shampoo. For this price, you can’t beat the quality.
ReviewContent: I have tried many dry shampoo’s, and Batiste is by far my favorite. This (the original) is my favorite scent although all their scents are great. It does an incredible job of soaking up oil and blending into the hair. No white residue and not a drop of oil after a few sprays on your roots. For reference, I’m a 35 year old Caucasian female with very thick, coarse hair (about 1-2 inches past the shoulder in length) that is naturally medium brown in color, although I do add blonde highlights every eight weeks or so. I only wash my hair once a week, and you would never guess that by looking at my hair on day seven. This dry shampoo also helps perk your blow out back up- it erases any creases that are caused when I clip back my hair while washing my face/brushing my teeth. I pin my hair back with a clip and use a shower cap when showering to keep my hair dry. I once had a boyfriend tell me that my hair was always “on point”, and it was shocking to him when he found out that I only wash it once weekly. He said I had the best smelling hair he had ever encountered as well. Batiste can be pricy when you buy a single can in the drugstore, but I always buy in bulk on Amazon. For the prices on here, you can’t beat the quality. This specific seller was very fast with shipping and the product was authentic.  I received my product tightly packed together in clear plastic. No issues or concerns.

ProductTitle: Batiste Dry Shampoo Fresh, Breezy Citrus Scent, Refreshes Hair Without Drying, 4.23 oz (Pack of 6)
ReviewTitle: Licensed cosmetologist, and this is my favorite dry shampoo.
ReviewContent: I am a licensed cosmetologist. I have tried so many different brands and kinds of dry shampoo. Professional and not. Yet this one, is the one I keep coming back to. It has a good smell, and it works well! It’s a decent price, and good quality for the price. Yes, there are better dry shampoos out there, but they have a much higher price point. And comparatively, I love this shampoo and it works as well as I need it to! It’s not worth paying a lot more for a slightly better product. I also use it way more often than I should be… so price is kind of a big deal for me. It’s good for oily hair, as well as adding extra body to your hair. It’s great. Sometimes leaves some white spots, but it’s avoidable, and easy enough to rub them out or hide them with a comb or brush and sometimes a little water. Other than that, I have no complaints.

ProductTitle: Death Wish Coffee Organic Dark Roast Ground Coffee, Fair Trade, 16 oz | Arabica & Robusta Blend, Baker's Chocolate & Cherry Notes, Low Acidity, Naturally High-Caffeine Robusta, Drip & French Press
ReviewTitle: Simply the best coffee I've ever tasted.
ReviewContent: I work in the medical field and as a result of my long shifts I tend to drink a lot of coffee and I mean a LOT of coffee. I like dark, strong, and black but since I pretty much rely on the beverage I'll usually just drink whatever I can get my hands on. I've tasted dozens of coffees from the cheap store brand to late night/early morning diner to some serious specialty brews and previously my favorite has always been the cheap diner coffee. Speaking of those specialty blends; they've always left something to be desired. There is a catch with them all - too weak, added flavors, sometimes just down right nasty. It was for that reason I was skeptical of Death Wish.Given those experiences, with my first pot I went conservative. Too conservative, to be honest. It was very watered down but even so I could taste something I suspected was great. It was smooth and rich. Definitely bitter but not biting. Sadly, since I brewed it at home and took it with me to work I didn't have a chance to try a stronger mix until this morning. I'm currently on my fifth cup and this time I went just a tad on the strong side. What are my thoughts? Well, let me tell you...5 Cups and still going is a lot of coffee and its not something most drinkers can't  relate to so most people would be thinking that I'm bouncing off the walls particularly since this is supposed to be ridiculously strong. Even with my tolerance one could easily expect that from me but I have bad news - the one thing I'd say negatively about this coffee is that the strength claims are perhaps, at best, overstated. Honestly, I can't feel any difference between and any other coffee in terms of caffeine. That is where my complaints end and as you can see, in spite of that, I still rated it 5 stars.The reason for that is simple: This is by far the best tasting coffee I've ever had. All of the things I detected in a weak pot carried over to the strong one. Heck, I even went a bit stronger than usual and its still not even a little harsh. Every sip I take amazes me because I cannot believe that something could taste so strong and rich without a bitter bite at the end but the truth is that there is none. Without question, it is truly amazing.I guess aside from the possibly overstated caffeine claims the biggest issue is price. Based on how much coffee I drink there is no way I can afford to make this my regular brew and as I would so very much want to do. There are plenty of people out there who make more money than I do and if you like coffee at all, regardless how you feel about strength, you should try this. If you do, please don't ruin it with creamer, sugar, milk, or any other additive before giving it a try black. I honestly believe that you'll find it to be better than any thing else you've ever tasted.

ProductTitle: Death Wish Coffee Organic Dark Roast Ground Coffee, Fair Trade, 16 oz | Arabica & Robusta Blend, Baker's Chocolate & Cherry Notes, Low Acidity, Naturally High-Caffeine Robusta, Drip & French Press
ReviewContent: TL;DR: Death Wish Coffee is good.So my sleep habits are not a mystery to anyone. I average about 4-4.5 hours of actual sleep a night (as opposed to just laying in bed thinking about everything, like math because I do that). Needless to say, I drag in the mornings.Enter Death Wish Coffee. I should note that I have tried this before, but it was at a bar and I was already a couple drinks in. It ships in a bag, inside a box, inside another box. Upon arrival I could smell it through the exterior box. The smell is strong but delightful, and I could tell it was going to be an experience.Comparing it to “regular” coffee is hardly fair. The aroma is stronger, the color richer, and quite a bit darker. Like. REALLY dark. I started the brewing process then stepped in the back to turn lights on and get ready for the day ahead. The scent of coffee immediately filled my office, the one across the hall, and the hallway with its perfume. This was a welcome development since my office generally smells awful. I think something may have died in the drop ceiling a room over. I’ve used a ladder to look up there and haven’t found anything; perhaps the smell is originating somewhere else. After pouring this in my mustache-protecting cup (nothing worse than having your facial hair soak up liquids) I could tell it was considerably darker than a regular roast or even other dark roasts. Not quite “used motor oil” black, but not too far off. Speaking of, I drink my coffee black the way it is intended to be drank. No fancy, organic, free trade, non-GMO, gluten free, crossfitting, vegan friendly, sugar or creamer for me. I should probably note that this coffee is “USDA Organic” certified by QAI US-ORG-050. Whatever that means.I can’t drink my coffee anywhere near the temperature of the Earths core, like some people I know, so I let it sit a minute to get to a drinkable temp. This gave me some time to fully appreciate the smell and, as a bonus, built the anticipation even higher.I was in no way, shape, or form prepared for the kick in the face that I was about to receive.Despite the smell, I expected this coffee to be bitter like most other coffees. Not the case. This was very smooth and not at all acidic tasting/feeling. I immediately felt my pulse quicken and my productivity levels increase. Drinking this on an empty stomach may not have been the “smartest” decision but the one I made and the one I had to live with.  I felt alive. With this newfound vigor I was able to complete all of my work for the day before 1100. I will spend the rest of the day waiting for FedEx or whoever to make their delivery. With the extra time I had on my hands I decided to see if my desire to work had increased or if my efficiency level was up as well. I did the only thing I knew to do, take a typing test.I type pretty quickly as it is, generally in the 85 wpm area. With all this energy, I was able to hit 124 wpm (at my fastest) and averaged 97 wpm throughout the typing test. Needless to say, I was pumped.This coffee is great. The only downside is that it is somewhat expensive. At $20 for a 1lb bag the cost may be a deterrent for most. However, a little bit goes a long way and they make K-cups for all you fancy pants people that know how to work a Keurig.Hmmm…this review has ended up being a little longer than anticipated and oddly enough longer than some papers I have written for school.
